Definition: Tachan, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Tachan is the name of two Israelites. One was a son of Ephraim, head of the family of the Tachanites in the census of the plains of Moab, and the other was a son of Telah in the genealogy of Ephraim in the Chronicler's list. The name is carried by a family, not by a story, and both men are known only by their sons and their tribe.
TheologicalSignificance: Ordinary fathers are honoured by the census names, I believe: a man can be known in Scripture only as the head of his family, and God counts the family anyway.
